Endpoints should return errors as RFC 7807 `problem+json` responses, built with `errors.problem(status, title, detail)` from `src/api/errors.py`. This is a stored project convention, and I confirmed the helper exists at `src/api/errors.py:4`. It sets the mimetype to `application/problem+json`.

The reason is that clients of the public API parse error bodies automatically, so every endpoint has to return the same shape. Don't return ad-hoc dicts or plain strings with an error status code.

```python
from src.api.errors import problem

return problem(404, "Invoice not found", "No invoice with id 123")
```

I didn't read `src/api/invoices.py` or `src/api/checkout.py`, so I haven't checked whether they follow this. A grep for `problem` in `src` found no call sites outside `errors.py`. The only `raise` statements are in `src/billing/`, in `refunds.py` (a `ValueError`) and `tax.py` (a `NotImplementedError`). Those errors would need to be caught and translated to `problem(...)` at the API layer. I didn't check whether that happens.
